newsitem.title: GERMANY: Veba/RWE's O.tel.o sees breakeven in five years.
newsitem.headline: Veba/RWE's O.tel.o sees breakeven in five years.

text.p: O.tel.o, the telecommmunications joint venture of utilities Veba AG and RWE AG, said on Thursday it expects to break even in five years.
It also plans to post annual revenue of 7-9 billion marks ($4.1-$5.3 billion) by 2005, without including revenue from E-plus, the mobile telephone company in which Veba holds a stake.
"We plan to reach the breakeven point within five years. To do that we are investing seven billion marks in the coming years," O.tel.o chairman Ulf Bohla told reporters at the Cebit technology fair.
The revenue projection corresponds to a share of 12 to 17 percent of the German market.
Three quarters of this business will be in voice communications, half of which will be in domestic and international long-distance traffic, Bohla said.
